rows.title: Corey Hutchins’ year in review: The news behind the news in Colorado’s media world in 2024
rows.standfirst: Rural newspapers and radio stations closed and lawmakers made state government less transparent

rows.title: Colorado’s job-growth incentive had lackluster 2024
rows.standfirst: Approved projects dropped by 34%, and the value of tax credits awarded and promised jobs fell by more than 70% from a year ago.

rows.title: What’s Working: What some Colorado economists expect in 2025 — and how they’re preparing for it
rows.standfirst: The uncertainty continues, as America waits for Trump’s pledges to raise tariffs, conduct mass deportations and slash spending. Plus: Colorado’s 5 minimum wages

rows.title: The good, the bad and the algorithm: What banning TikTok could do to Colorado creators
rows.standfirst: TikTok has become a gathering space for all kinds of niche interests, but with a looming ban, local creators and consumers fear they could lose access to their communities.

rows.title: Former eye bank workers say pressure, lax oversight led to errors in Colorado, Wyoming
rows.standfirst: Rocky Mountain Lions Eye Bank estimates it collects eye tissue from about 2,500 deceased donors a year. Four ex-employees say there is a tense work environment resulting in damaged or wasted tissues due to accidents.

rows.title: United Airlines settles racial discrimination lawsuit in case of ex-Denver employee
rows.standfirst: A manager at the airline’s catering facility used a racial slur with an Asian American employee and is no longer at United, which agreed to pay $99,000 plus other relief

rows.title: 2025 will be the year of the budget cut at the Colorado Capitol
rows.standfirst: The Colorado legislature reconvenes in Denver on Wednesday to kick off its 120-day legislative session facing, by one estimate, a $750 million budget shortfall

rows.title: Homelessness among families with children in Colorado grew by 134% in 2024, according to federal report
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Housing and Urban Development report reveals that Colorado was one of four states where family homelessness more than doubled

rows.title: Vail Resorts, ski patrollers reach an agreement that could end strike at Park City Mountain Resort
rows.standfirst: Patrollers at the largest ski area in the country were seeking increased pay when they went on strike Dec. 27, leaving Park City Mountain unable to open terrain during the busy, snowy holiday

rows.title: New midstream gas rules should cut greenhouse emissions, Colorado officials say
rows.standfirst: Environmental groups object a December vote lacks enforcement, creates a questionable credit-trading system

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado companies show sweet tech at this year’s CES expo in Las Vegas
rows.standfirst: From neural haptics to an electric RV trailer, Colorado companies are still making cool tech. Plus: Local startup news, poll results, and more!

rows.title: Naropa University forced to break ties with its own psychedelic studies program, spawning new independent healing center
rows.standfirst: The Boulder institution will shed its groundbreaking Center for Psychedelic Studies into the collaborative, independent Memoru Center for Visionary Healing Arts

rows.title: Kansas looks on as farms retire thousands of acres in water-short northeastern Colorado
rows.standfirst: With the help of $30M in state and federal funding, it has retired some 10,000 acres of irrigated farm lands, with another 7,000 acres contracted for dry up

rows.title: What’s Working: What’s behind downtown Denver’s 34.9% office vacancy rate?
rows.standfirst: That’s higher than a year earlier. At least leasing has picked up to fill more office buildings this year. The city also has big things planned to change the vacancy trajectory in 2025.

rows.title: Many states have resisted nuclear waste storage plans. Northwestern Colorado is quietly opening the door.
rows.standfirst: As nuclear waste piles up around the country, many communities are saying “no” to taking it. In a rural corner of Colorado, however, some see the prospect of storing this spent fuel as an opportunity.

rows.title: Nonrenewals are fueling Colorado’s growing homeowners insurance crisis
rows.standfirst: In Colorado, homeowners’ premiums are up nearly 60% in five years. But the state is also dealing with insurers dropping coverage or leaving the state altogether.

rows.title: Jared Polis reveals his stance on the gun, labor and housing bills before the Colorado legislature this year
rows.standfirst: The Democrat was interviewed during the The Colorado Sun’s event previewing the 2025 legislative session

rows.title: Why disaster mitigation can protect your house, but may not lower your insurance bill — yet
rows.standfirst: As Colorado’s insurer of last resort comes online, new technology and upcoming legislation could make rising insurance premiums finally reflect efforts to lower risk

rows.title: King Soopers union sets first strike vote for Front Range stores, which could involve 10,000 workers
rows.standfirst: If workers vote to approve a strike, the walkout will involve more stores and employees than the nine-day strike in 2022.

rows.title: With Biden-era consumer protections in jeopardy, Colorado Democrats look to crack down on rental housing fees
rows.standfirst: The effort got a boost last week from a top Federal Trade Commission official, who sent a letter to Gov. Jared Polis urging the state to target so-called “junk fees”

rows.title: A fight over 340B, the federal program to help hospitals with prescription drug costs, is coming to the Colorado Capitol
rows.standfirst: The program helps boost revenue for hospitals that treat a lot of Medicaid patients. Advocates for and against are lobbying ahead of a legislative battle.

rows.title: A 62-year-old Denver man’s journey from home, to homeless, to a new apartment
rows.standfirst: Ronnie Hoover, suffering from heart and kidney problems, was a chef until he lost his job during the pandemic

rows.title: How Donald Trump’s return-to-office order will affect the 45,000 federal employees throughout Colorado
rows.standfirst: At least 44,500 federal workers are in Colorado. According to federal data, most work in-person at the office some or all of the work week.

rows.title: Dana Crawford, credited with saving Denver’s Larimer Square from destruction, dies at 93
rows.standfirst: Crawford stopped urban renewal that rolled through Denver in the 1960s on her block, and then committed to the preservation and adaptive reuse of buildings from Trinidad to Idaho Springs

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado has a new climate-jobs coalition, as Trump pulls back on green energy
rows.standfirst: Colorado Climate Jobs wants high-quality union jobs, lower costs for working families and a clean energy economy that works for Coloradans. Are they possible under the new administration?

rows.title: Are employers in Colorado required to pay workers for unused vacation time?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Earned vacation time is protected under the Colorado Wage Act, which prohibits use-it-or-lose-it policies in the workplace.

rows.title: Colorado’s unemployment rate rises to 4.4%, the highest in three years
rows.standfirst: New business filings have flattened and job openings have declined, as the number of Coloradans in the labor force hit a record high.

rows.title: 107 oil and gas wells owned by a company based in a Highlands Ranch home are about to land on Colorado’s orphan list
rows.standfirst: The wells, most of which are on federal land, are not producing and have been passed from company to company, racking up environmental violations.

rows.title: Replacing mining with nuclear waste? Northwestern Colorado has mixed feelings about how to save the economy.
rows.standfirst: As northwestern Colorado loses coal jobs, a group is raising the possibility of nuclear waste storage as a replacement. People around Hayden aren’t sure this is the “just transition” they want.

rows.title: Denver-based Frontier Airlines makes a second bid for Spirit as budget airlines struggle
rows.standfirst: Spirit said almost immediately that it’s not interested in the sale, and an attempted merger between the two airlines came to nothing in 2022

rows.title: Denver-area King Soopers workers vote to strike over unfair labor practices
rows.standfirst: Pueblo and Colorado Springs workers vote next. UFCW Local 7 represents 12,000 King Soopers and City Market workers in Colorado.
